subject.title: [Bug]: Extension plugins silently skipped by gateway loader in v5.3+ (loads in CLI process, not in long-running daemon)

question: Should OpenClaw restore Gateway startup loading for explicitly enabled legacy non-bundled hook plugins without activation metadata, and what opt-out or diagnostic safeguards are required?
rationale: The issue is a real regression for security/audit hooks, but the repair affects when native non-bundled plugin code executes inside the long-running Gateway process.

options.title: Restore compatible startup with safeguards
options.body: Treat explicit enabled-plus-allowed legacy hook plugins as startup candidates while preserving deny lists, `enabled: false`, explicit startup opt-outs, and adding focused daemon proof.

options.title: Require activation metadata
options.body: Keep the stricter activation contract and close the runtime request only after docs, doctor, and warnings make the failure mode loud and actionable.

options.title: Ship diagnostics first
options.body: Add Gateway/doctor warnings for skipped configured hook plugins before deciding whether legacy startup compatibility should return.

recommendation.title: Restore compatible startup with safeguards
recommendation.body: Treat explicit enabled-plus-allowed legacy hook plugins as startup candidates while preserving deny lists, `enabled: false`, explicit startup opt-outs, and adding focused daemon proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent startup metadata planning work plus repository security/compatibility policy make this the best available owner for the security-boundary choice.
